meta.description: Human-reviewed contributor queue. The bot reads this file and nothing else. Every entry is reviewed in a normal pull request, which is the point: an agent that decides at runtime what to build will duplicate, hallucinate, and file issues nobody can action.
notes: status: backlog    -> eligible only when complete and not explicitly gated; ready items come first
status: ready      -> eligible; the bot may file it when the cap allows
status: filed      -> the bot created it; the marker lives in the issue body
status: shipped    -> the bot may comment + close its own issue, naming the release
Only ready/backlog entries with complete bodies and auto_file not false are ever filed.
latest_release   -> the tag the close comment cites; empty means the bot will not close anything it filed
auto_file: false -> explicit maintainer gate; never filed automatically even if body is complete.
Ready tasks are preferred; complete ungated backlog tasks replenish available slots. Historical markers prevent re-filing closed work.

Maintainer authorized up to 20 open contributor tasks total; roadmap and growth publishers share the ceiling. The cap bounds how much work is on the board at once, not how often it files: every closed issue opens the next eligible one at the hourly run.
There are no dates. An item opens when its depends_on IDs are shipped (or a closed issue carries its marker) — that is the only ordering rule, and it fails closed on a missing id.
Agentic roadmap items file as soon as their prerequisites are shipped and a slot is free; caps, queue priority and historical dedupe still apply, and nothing waits for a calendar.
Four-repository extension: harness-* tasks reuse agentic-* prerequisites under the same hourly caps and shipped gates.
not_before is refused by scripts/validate-roadmap.js: a schedule the queue does not read is worse than no schedule at all.

- [ ] Passes on Node 22, 24 and 26
- [ ] Test name states the guarantee, not the implementation

```bash
node --test test/hardening.test.js
node --test
node scripts/audit.js
```

~2-3 hours.

items.title: fix(growth): normalize GitHub OPEN/CLOSED issue states before planning
items.body:
## Context

**Confirmed deterministic planner bug**, not a feature proposal. At baseline 7337971, plan() filters existing issues using state === "open". gh issue list --json uses uppercase OPEN/CLOSED, while REST uses lowercase. items.title: feat(voice): measure and hold an end-to-end voice latency budget
items.verify:
node --test test/audio-input.test.js test/agent.test.js
node --test --test-concurrency=4 && node scripts/audit.js
items.body:
## Context

`src/telemetry.js` already records a per-turn duration and reports p50/p95, but it cannot say *where* a slow turn was slow. A voice request has five stages — capture end → endpoint decision → final transcript → first token → first audio — and only the total is recorded. "It feels laggy" is therefore unactionable, and any speed claim in the README would be unprovable today.

The budget this item exists to enforce: endpoint ≤300 ms after the speaker stops, final transcript ≤300 ms after endpoint, first token ≤700 ms on a local 7B model, first audio ≤1.2 s from end of speech.

## What to change

- `src/telemetry.js`: add a `stages` object to each record — `captureEndMs`, `endpointMs`, `transcriptMs`, `firstTokenMs`, `firstAudioMs` — relative to one turn start. Never record transcript text, prompts or audio.
- `src/server.js`: emit the stage marks it owns (request received, first SSE delta written) on the existing stream; do not add a second endpoint.
- `public/cosmic.js`: mark the browser-owned stages (capture stop, recognition final) and POST them with the turn, best-effort — a missing mark is `null`, never `0`, because a fabricated zero reads as a perfect score.
- `quasnooze health --json`: include per-stage p50/p95 over the telemetry ring, with the sample count next to each so a p95 of four turns is visibly weak evidence.
- `docs/VOICE.md`: a budget table naming each stage, its target, and the fact that these are local measurements on one machine — not a cross-device benchmark.

**Safety:** measurement only. It must not add a network call, a timer that keeps a process alive, or a second audio stream.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A turn with no browser stages still records its server stages; missing stages are `null`, not `0`
- [ ] No message text, transcript, prompt, or audio bytes appear in `telemetry.ndjson` (asserted, not reviewed)
- [ ] `quasnooze health --json` reports p50/p95 per stage with sample counts
- [ ] The docs table lists a target for every stage it reports

## How to verify

```bash
node --test test/audio-input.test.js
grep -c 'transcript\"' data/telemetry.ndjson  # must be 0
node scripts/doctor.js --json | head -40
```

## Time estimate

~4-6 hours

items.body:
## Context

Today the only local speech path is a whole-clip POST: `src/voice.js` sends a finished file to a Whisper-compatible endpoint with a 5 s deadline and gets text back once. Browser `SpeechRecognition` produces partials, but it is a separate path that **may send audio to the browser vendor** (`docs/VOICE.md` says so explicitly), so "fast" and "local" are currently different products.

Nothing decides when the user has finished speaking. Without that, every turn waits for a silence timer in the UI, which is what makes a local assistant feel slower than it measures.

## What to change

- `public/audio-input.js`: add a VAD/endpointing stage over the existing `AnalyserNode` graph — speech onset, trailing silence, and a maximum utterance cap. No new dependency, no ML model.
- Stream partial transcripts from the local path: chunked uploads to the Whisper-compatible endpoint (or a local streaming server if configured), with the previous chunk's context passed as `prompt`.
- `public/cosmic.js`: render partials as provisional text and mark them clearly as partial in the `role="status"` live region; never let a partial enter conversation history.
- `docs/VOICE.md`: state which path is local, which may leave the device, and what endpointing does and does not guarantee.

**Safety:** audio analysis stays in the page; no recording is persisted, and the cloud-recognition path stays opt-in and labelled.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Endpoint fires within the configured window on synthetic silence, tested with a fixture, not a microphone
- [ ] A partial transcript never becomes a stored message; only the final one does
- [ ] Denial, missing device and busy device still produce actionable messages
- [ ] Disabling streaming falls back to the current whole-clip path with no behavioural difference


## Context

- Record the interruption in telemetry as its own outcome so the rate is visible (`outcome: "interrupted"`), separate from `STREAM_CUT`.

- [ ] Speech during playback stops audio, marks the turn interrupted, and aborts the provider request

## Context

`system_control` currently exposes exactly two actions, `lock` and `sleep`, and shutdown is deliberately absent. Everything a person actually says to a computer — "turn it down", "mute", "pause" — is missing, so the assistant is a chat box on a machine it cannot touch.

These actions are the safest possible expansion of that tool: bounded, idempotent, reversible, and obvious from the outside.

## What to change

- `src/tools.js`: extend `system_control` with `volume_up`, `volume_down`, `set_volume`, `mute`, `unmute`, `media_play_pause`, `media_next`, `media_previous` — each with explicit parameters and a typed result.

- `src/risk.js`: classify these as `act` (approval) but non-destructive, so approval can be granted for a session rather than every press.
- Clamp `set_volume` to 0-100 and return the resulting level, so a follow-up “how loud is it?” has an answer.

**Safety:** no shell interpolation. Parameters are numbers and enums only.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Every action returns the resulting state (muted, level) rather than `ok`
- [ ] `set_volume 500` is rejected with a bounded error, not clamped silently to 100
- [ ] On platforms without a host, the tool returns a typed failure and the assistant says so

node --test test/hardening.test.js test/tools.test.js
node --test --test-concurrency=4 && node scripts/audit.js
items.body:
## Context

"Tidy my downloads" is the request that makes a voice assistant feel useful, and it is also a request nobody should grant to an LLM without a way back. Today file operations are `write_file` inside the workspace and nothing else; there is no move, no rename, no trash, and no record of what changed.

`src/guard.js` already confines writes to the workspace root. This extends that discipline rather than relaxing it: every mutation is journaled, previewed, and reversible.

## What to change

- `src/tools.js`: `move_path`, `rename_path`, `trash_path` restricted to configured roots, refusing to cross roots and refusing to overwrite without an explicit flag.
- A journal entry per mutation (source, destination, timestamp, turn id) written through `src/store.js`, with `undo_last` and `list_recent_changes`.
- Batch preview: a plan of N operations is shown once and approved once, and the journal keeps the batch id so undo reverses the whole plan.
- `trash_path` moves to a local trash directory, never a hard delete; nothing in this item can unlink.

**Safety:** reversibility is the feature. If undo cannot restore the state, the operation is not offered.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] No operation can delete; trash is recoverable and undo restores the original path
- [ ] Cross-root moves are refused, not silently copied
- [ ] Undo of a partially-applied batch reports exactly what was restored
- [ ] Every mutation appears in the journal and in the approval preview before it runs

## How to verify

```bash
node --test test/hardening.test.js test/tools.test.js
node --test --test-concurrency=4 && node scripts/audit.js
```

## Time estimate

~2-3 days

items.title: feat(voice): opt-in local wake gating that is not authentication
items.verify:
node --test test/desktop.test.js test/audio-input.test.js
node --test --test-concurrency=4 && node scripts/audit.js
items.body:
## Context

The Windows host supports an opt-in "Hey Quasnooze" phrase through `System.Speech`, but the browser path has no gating at all: the visualizer analyses audio the moment the user enables the microphone, and there is no way to say "listen for one phrase, not for everything".

A wake phrase is a **convenience trigger, not a security boundary** — recorded audio can replay it. The README already says so. This item makes the convenience real without pretending it is a lock.

## What to change

- `public/audio-input.js`: an on-device wake gate that runs before transcription, using a local keyword match on the recognition result rather than streaming audio anywhere.
- Explicit states: `gate-idle`, `gate-heard`, `listening`, `sending` — surfaced in the UI so a person can see which one is active at any moment.
- `docs/VOICE.md`: a paragraph stating plainly that a wake phrase is not authentication and does not protect against a recording.
- Off by default, per-surface opt-in, and released on page hide like every other capture path.

**Safety:** the phrase decides *when to listen*, never *who is allowed*. No approval gate may be keyed to it.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Audio is not sent to any model until the gate fires
- [ ] The UI always shows whether the gate is armed, and it is off by default
- [ ] No documentation or UI copy implies the phrase authenticates the speaker
- [ ] Hiding or navigating away releases the microphone

## How to verify

```bash
node --test test/desktop.test.js test/audio-input.test.js
node --test --test-concurrency=4
```

## Time estimate

~2-3 days

items.title: feat(agent): plan multi-step work and verify before claiming success
items.verify:
node --test test/agent.test.js test/batch2.test.js
node --test --test-concurrency=4 && node scripts/audit.js
items.body:
## Context

A multi-tool turn currently streams whatever the model says after the last tool call. There is no check that the stated outcome matches the tool results, so "Done — I moved all twelve files" can follow a single successful move.

`src/agent.js` has the tool results in hand at the end of a turn. The honest version of this feature is small: make the assistant answer from the receipts it actually has.

## What to change

- Before a turn that needs three or more tool calls, produce a short plan and show it in the transcript as a plan — not as an answer.
- After the last tool call, build a receipt set (tool name, target, result, count) and refuse to state an outcome that the receipts do not support; the honesty guard in `src/prompt.js` is the natural place for the forbidden phrasing.
- Partial failure is reported per step (`3 of 12 moved; 9 failed: …`) instead of summarised as success.
- No plan is stored as memory, and a plan is not an approval for anything it lists.

**Safety:** verification reads tool results; it must never invent one, and must not be able to approve anything.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A claim of N completed operations with fewer than N successful results is blocked or corrected
- [ ] Partial failures list the failed items
- [ ] Plans never authorise a tool call; each still passes the risk classifier
- [ ] Existing honesty-guard tests still pass

## How to verify

```bash
node --test test/agent.test.js test/batch2.test.js
node --test --test-concurrency=4 && node scripts/audit.js
```

## Time estimate

~2-3 days

items.title: feat(agent): validate tool arguments against their schema and repair once
items.verify:
node --test test/tools.test.js test/agent.test.js
node --test --test-concurrency=4 && node scripts/audit.js
items.body:
## Context

Every tool in `src/tools.js` declares a `parameters` schema and then trusts whatever the model produced. A missing required field surfaces as a stack trace or a `TypeError` deep inside a handler, which is both a bad answer and a bad bug report.

A validator plus a single repair round turns the most common local-model failure — malformed arguments — into a recoverable event.

## What to change

- A dependency-free validator for the subset of JSON Schema the tools already use (`type`, `required`, `enum`, `properties`, primitives, arrays).
- On failure, one repair round: return the validation errors to the model and let it retry once, then fail with a typed `BAD_TOOL_ARGS` result.
- Never coerce a wrong type silently; report it. `set_volume: "loud"` is an error, not a zero.
- The typed failure appears in the transcript as a sentence a person can act on.

**Safety:** validation narrows what the model can do. It must never relax a risk tier or fabricate a default.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Unknown tool names, missing required fields and wrong types all produce `BAD_TOOL_ARGS`
- [ ] Exactly one repair attempt happens, and it is visible in telemetry
- [ ] A valid call is passed through byte-identically to today's behaviour
- [ ] No new runtime dependency

## How to verify

```bash
node --test test/tools.test.js test/agent.test.js
node --test --test-concurrency=4
```

## Time estimate

~3-5 hours

items.title: feat(agent): shape tool-call arguments at sampling time, not after
items.verify:
node --test test/agent.test.js test/tools.test.js
node --test --test-concurrency=4 && node scripts/audit.js
items.body:
## Context

A malformed tool call is currently discovered after the fact: `src/agent.js` parses the arguments, and when parsing fails it spends a whole model round trip answering *"Your arguments were not valid JSON … Re-emit"*. That round trip is the most expensive possible way to fix a comma.

Local runtimes can make the failure mechanically impossible instead: Ollama accepts a full JSON Schema in the `format` field and constrains decoding with xgrammar, giving effectively total schema compliance. `reason-02` catches what the model gets wrong; this item means a smaller share of it is ever wrong, and the repair round becomes the rare fallback rather than the expected path.

## What to change

- Build the schema once per tool from the existing `TOOLS` definitions (single source of truth — no second copy of the shape), flattening where the runtime's supported subset requires it.
- Send it as `format` on tool-deciding turns for the Ollama provider; leave non-tool turns free-form so answers keep their voice.
- Keep `reason-02`'s validation and single repair exactly as they are: constrained decoding is defence in depth, not a replacement for checking.
- Emit a telemetry counter for constrained calls, malformed-argument rate and repairs, so the claim is measured per model — small local models vary enormously here.
- `docs/ROUTING.md`: which providers get the constraint, and what happens on a provider that does not support it.

**Safety:** the schema constrains **shape only**. It cannot widen a risk tier, pre-approve a call or skip the action preview: a perfectly-shaped `write_file` still goes through the same approval gate as a malformed one.

## Performance contract

- **Baseline:** not implemented — arguments are free text parsed after the fact, and every malformed call costs a full repair round trip (the `Re-emit` path in `src/agent.js`); malformed rate is not currently recorded
- **Target:** malformed tool arguments under **1% of calls** on the tool-call corpus (from a recorded per-model baseline), with repair round trips for schema-shaped errors down to zero
- **Must not regress:** a model or provider that ignores the constraint must still get the existing validation and repair path; no tool schema may be loosened to make compliance easier; per-call overhead stays within +50 ms

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Schemas are generated from `TOOLS`, not hand-copied
- [ ] Malformed rate and repair count are recorded per model before and after
- [ ] A provider without support degrades to today's behaviour, unchanged
- [ ] `reason-02` validation and repair tests still pass untouched
- [ ] A shaped-but-unsafe call (write outside the workspace, `act` tier) is still refused by the risk tier

## How to verify

```bash
node --test test/agent.test.js test/tools.test.js
node --test --test-concurrency=4 && node scripts/audit.js
```

## Time estimate

~4-6 days

items.verify:

node --test --test-concurrency=4 && node scripts/audit.js
items.body:
## Context

`screenshot` exists, but nothing turns a screenshot into an actionable element. When the user says "click Export" and no tool knows what "Export" is, the assistant has no way to find out — which is exactly the case a desktop assistant is expected to handle.

The disciplined version: one screenshot, on demand, local OCR or accessibility tree first, coordinates shown to the user before any click.

## What to change

- `desktop/Companion.cs`: expose the UI Automation tree (name, control type, bounding rectangle) alongside the existing screenshot; OCR is a fallback, not the first choice.
- `src/tools.js`: `find_on_screen(text)` returns ranked candidates with their rectangle and owning window — and nothing else. Clicking is a separate, approved tool.
- A click tool requires a fresh approval that names the element text and the window; a stale match (window changed) fails instead of clicking somewhere new.
- Everything local by default: no screenshot leaves the machine unless the user configured a vision provider and approved that specific call.

**Safety:** a click is irreversible from the assistant's side. Fresh approval, named target, no replay.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Element search returns candidates with window and rectangle, never a bare coordinate
- [ ] A click is refused when the owning window is not the approved one
- [ ] No screenshot is uploaded to a provider without per-call, explicit consent
- [ ] Works with no vision model configured, using the accessibility tree alone

## How to verify

```bash
node --test test/desktop.test.js test/scan.test.js
node --test --test-concurrency=4 && node scripts/audit.js
```

~4-6 days

items.title: test(voice): a labelled speech corpus and command-accuracy report
items.verify:
node --test test/speech-accuracy.test.js
node scripts/evaluate-speech.js
node --test --test-concurrency=4 && node scripts/audit.js
items.body:
## Context

The README says voice accuracy has not been measured on physical hardware, and that is still true: there is no corpus, no word-error-rate number and no command-accuracy number. Any future "it understands you better now" claim would therefore be an opinion.

The retrieval side of this repository already sets the pattern — a labelled local corpus and a reproducible report (`docs/RETRIEVAL-EVALUATION.md`). Speech deserves the same.

## What to change

- A small, redistributable corpus of short command utterances: clean, accented, noisy, and numbers/names, with a licence that permits publishing the text and the expected transcript.
- A runner that scores word error rate and, separately, **command accuracy** — did the transcript select the intended tool with the intended arguments.
- Report per condition, with sample counts, and refuse to print a headline number when a condition has fewer than a stated minimum of samples.
- `docs/VOICE.md`: the report location, the method, and the fact that synthetic or replayed audio is not hardware acceptance.

**Safety:** the corpus must contain no recordings of real people without consent, and no private data.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The runner is deterministic and offline; no model download at test time
- [ ] Command accuracy is measured separately from WER, because a plausible transcript can still pick the wrong tool
- [ ] Every reported number carries its sample count
- [ ] The docs distinguish measured results from unperformed physical-microphone checks

## How to verify

```bash
node --test test/voice.test.js
node --test --test-concurrency=4 && node scripts/audit.js
```

## Where it landed

`scripts/evaluate-speech.js` scores the corpus in `test-fixtures/speech/v1/corpus.json` (48 hand-authored utterances, CC0-1.0, no audio) and writes `docs/SPEECH-BASELINE-V1.md`. Word error rate and command accuracy are reported separately, each with its sample count; a condition under `MIN_CONDITION_SAMPLES` (8) reports withheld, and so does the headline. `npm run health` prints the corpus size and whether the committed baseline is still current. The hypotheses are authored text, so this is not hardware acceptance — that boundary is stated in `docs/VOICE.md`.

## Time estimate

~2-3 days

items.title: feat(voice): clarify instead of guessing when a transcript is ambiguous
items.verify:
node --test test/agent.test.js test/assistant-text.test.js
node --test --test-concurrency=4 && node scripts/audit.js
items.body:
## Context

Speech is lossy in a way typed text is not: "close the window" and "close the window in Photoshop" differ by one clause and by a hundred percent of the blast radius. Today a low-confidence transcript goes to the model as if it were certain.

A short clarification is faster than an undo, and it is the difference between an assistant that guesses and one that is trusted with the laptop.

## What to change

- Carry a confidence signal from the recognizer where the platform provides one, and treat a missing signal as unknown — never as confident.
- When a dangerous tool (`type_text`, `close_window`, `trash_path`, shell `act`) is about to run from low-confidence or very short input, ask one bounded question with the two most likely readings.
- Never ask more than one question per turn, and never ask for a read-only action.
- Log the clarification event (not the text) so the rate is measurable.

**Safety:** clarifying must not soften the approval gate. A confirmed reading still needs approval.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A dangerous action from low-confidence input produces exactly one clarifying question
- [ ] A read-only action never triggers a clarification
- [ ] The chosen reading is echoed before the action runs, so a wrong pick is visible
- [ ] Unknown confidence is treated as unknown, not as high

## How to verify

```bash
node --test test/agent.test.js test/assistant-text.test.js
node --test --test-concurrency=4
```

## Time estimate

~1-2 days

items.title: feat(os): user-defined voice shortcuts that expand to approved tool chains
items.verify:
node --test test/custom-tools.test.js test/tools.test.js
node --test --test-concurrency=4 && node scripts/audit.js
items.body:
## Context

People say the same six things to their computer every morning: open the work windows, set the volume, start the timer. Today each of those is a fresh model turn with fresh variance, which is both slower and less predictable than it needs to be.

A macro is a named list of tool calls the user wrote and approved once. It removes the model from the hot path without removing the user from the decision.

## What to change

- A JSON macro file next to the existing custom-tool config: `name`, `phrases`, ordered `calls` with literal arguments, and whether the whole macro is pre-approved.
- `src/tools.js`: `run_macro(name)` — arguments are literal from the file, never model-supplied; a macro cannot take a free-text parameter in this iteration.
- Anything destructive inside a macro still raises a per-call approval; pre-approval covers only the reversible actions named at definition time.
- Exact-phrase matching runs before the model, so a recognised macro skips inference entirely and says so.

**Safety:** pre-approval is scoped to the exact calls defined, and revocable by editing one file.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A macro's arguments come from the file, never from the transcript
- [ ] A destructive step inside a macro still asks, every time
- [ ] Unknown macro names fall through to normal conversation
- [ ] Skipping inference is visible in the transcript and in telemetry

## How to verify

```bash

```

~2-3 days

items.title: feat(voice): keep context across voice turns and resolve what was just said
items.verify:
node --test test/agent.test.js test/personas.test.js
node --test --test-concurrency=4 && node scripts/audit.js
items.body:
## Context

"Do it again" and "the second one" are how people talk, and they require the assistant to know what "it" and "the second one" were. The store already keeps sessions and memory, but referents from the previous turn — the window it just focused, the file it just moved — are not carried forward.

This is the difference between a voice assistant you repeat yourself to and one you talk to.

## What to change

- `src/store.js`: a small per-session referent table (last target per tool family, last list shown, last error) with an expiry, written only for actions the user actually took.
- `src/agent.js`: include the referents in the prompt as structured context, clearly labelled as what happened, not as instructions from the model.
- `src/prompt.js`: forbid inventing a referent when none is present — "the second one" with no prior list must ask.
- Deleting a session deletes its referents; nothing here is long-term memory.

**Safety:** carrying a referent is not permission; the same approval rules apply to the repeated action.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A referent is never offered when the previous turn did not establish one
- [ ] "Do it again" repeats the last action only after a fresh approval where the action is destructive
- [ ] Session deletion removes referents
- [ ] Referents never appear in telemetry or a support bundle

## How to verify

```bash

node --test --test-concurrency=4 && node scripts/audit.js
```

~2-3 days

items.title: feat(voice): record a per-stage latency waterfall on every turn
items.verify:
node --test test/readiness.test.js test/voice.test.js
node --test --test-concurrency=4 && node scripts/audit.js
items.body:
## Context

`src/telemetry.js` records a turn's total duration, its tool rounds and its token count. The budget in `docs/VOICE-CONTROL-ROADMAP.md` §5 is written per stage — endpoint, transcript, first token, first audio — but nothing records those stages, so a regression can only be found as "it feels slower".

The local-voice projects that are actually usable treat the pipeline as separate services with separate clocks: Home Assistant's Wyoming path publishes an expected latency per stage and its community measures exactly that. The lesson is not the protocol; it is that a pipeline you cannot break down is a pipeline you cannot tune.

## What to change

- Five timestamps per turn with stable names: `endOfSpeech`, `finalTranscript`, `firstToken`, `firstAudio`, `done`. Missing stages are recorded as missing, never as zero.
- Persist per-turn stage durations (durations only, no text, no audio) into the existing telemetry store, with a rolling p50/p95 per stage over the last 50 turns.
- `npm run health` prints the waterfall and names the slowest stage, with the sample count.
- A CI-friendly check that a stage regression above 20% against the committed baseline fails loudly.
- `docs/DIAGNOSTICS.md`: how to read a waterfall, and why a missing stage is different from a fast stage.

**Safety:** durations and stage names only — no transcript, no audio, no file paths. Everything stays in the local telemetry file, and the recorder cannot block a turn: if writing fails, the turn proceeds.

## Performance contract

- **Baseline:** partial — `src/telemetry.js` records total turn ms, rounds and tokens; the five stage boundaries exist only as a written budget, with 0 stages persisted per turn
- **Target:** 5 stage timings persisted for **100%** of voice turns, p50/p95 available per stage at n >= 50, recorder overhead **<= 5 ms** per turn
- **Must not regress:** the recorder may never drop, delay or reorder a turn, may never record text or audio content, and a blocked write must degrade to a missing stage rather than a failed request

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Every voice turn yields five timestamps or an explicit `missing` marker
- [ ] `npm run health` prints the waterfall with sample counts and the slowest stage
- [ ] A 20% regression in any stage fails the check
- [ ] No transcript or audio content appears in the telemetry file (asserted by test)
- [ ] Overhead is measured at 5 ms or less per turn
- [ ] Disabling the waterfall restores today's telemetry exactly

## How to verify

```bash
node --test test/readiness.test.js test/voice.test.js
node --test --test-concurrency=4 && node scripts/audit.js
```

## Time estimate

~3-5 days

items.title: feat(voice): semantic end-of-turn detection, not a silence timer
items.verify:
node --test test/audio-input.test.js test/voice.test.js
node --test --test-concurrency=4 && node scripts/audit.js
items.body:
## Context

LiveKit ships semantic turn detection as a first-class feature because silence is a bad proxy for "finished": people pause mid-sentence, and they also stop talking without pausing. Every silence-only endpointing scheme therefore picks one failure and lives with it — either it cuts people off or it makes them wait a full timeout after every clause. Our `voice-02` adds VAD endpointing, which is the floor, not the ceiling.

## What to change

- A small on-device classifier over features we already have: trailing-silence length, recent speech rate, whether the partial transcript ends in a conjunction/preposition/article, and pitch drop from the existing analyser.
- Two outputs, not one: `likelyDone` and `confidence`. The UI renders the listening state from them, so a person can see it is still waiting.
- A hard timeout ceiling (~1.5 s) so the model can never hold a turn open indefinitely.
- `docs/VOICE.md`: which layers decide the endpoint, and that this is a heuristic, not comprehension.

**Safety:** a wrong endpoint is worse than a slow one. When confidence is low, wait — never guess faster.

## Performance contract

- **Baseline:** not implemented — no semantic signal; endpointing is a fixed silence window (whatever `voice-02` settles on), and every mid-sentence pause costs the full window
- **Target:** false end-of-turn under 8% on the labelled corpus while median endpoint latency falls to 250 ms or less at the same cut-off rate
- **Must not regress:** must not increase the cut-off rate (turns ended while the speaker was still going) versus the fixed-window baseline

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Classification uses only local features; no audio or text leaves the machine
- [ ] The 1.5 s ceiling holds even when the classifier is uncertain
- [ ] Disabling the classifier restores exact `voice-02` behaviour
- [ ] The corpus report publishes cut-off and false-end rates side by side

## How to verify

```bash
node --test test/audio-input.test.js test/voice.test.js
node scripts/doctor.js --json | head -30
```

## Time estimate

~4-6 days

items.title: feat(voice): speak the first clause before the answer is finished
items.verify:
node --test test/voice.test.js test/voice-reply.test.js
node --test --test-concurrency=4 && node scripts/audit.js
items.body:
## Context

"Speak while the model is still writing" is how every low-latency assistant gets its first sound out in under a second, and it is the single biggest gap between a local assistant and a hosted one. Today the text streams (SSE deltas) but nothing is synthesised until the whole answer exists, so a fast local model still produces a slow-feeling assistant.

## What to change

- Sentence- and clause-level chunking of the stream: synthesise each chunk as it completes, queue playback, never re-synthesise.
- Chunk boundary rules that avoid mid-word and mid-number breaks ("1" + ".5", "New" + "York"), with a small lookahead buffer.
- Cancellation wiring to `voice-03`: an interrupted turn drops queued chunks immediately.
- `docs/VOICE.md`: that first-audio latency is chunked and that the full text may arrive after the first sound.

**Safety:** synthesis is local. No chunk and no text may be sent to a cloud TTS endpoint without the same per-call consent as any other off-device data.

## Performance contract

- **Baseline:** not implemented — first audio only after the complete answer exists, so on a 3-sentence reply it is the whole generation time
- **Target:** first audio 250 ms or less after the first token, with no mid-word break in a 200-case chunking suite
- **Must not regress:** must not regress total speech duration or the barge-in stop time (150 ms)

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Chunking never splits a number, an abbreviation or an inline code span
- [ ] An interrupted turn produces no audio after the stop signal
- [ ] Typed-only users see no change to text streaming
- [ ] The suite asserts chunk joins reconstruct the original text exactly

## How to verify

```bash
node --test test/voice.test.js test/voice-reply.test.js
node --test --test-concurrency=4
```

## Time estimate

~4-6 days

items.title: perf(voice): start the model on the partial transcript and discard a bad guess
items.verify:
node --test test/agent.test.js test/router.test.js
node --test --test-concurrency=4 && node scripts/audit.js
items.body:
## Context

A local 7B model spends most of its time-to-first-token in prefill, and prefill cannot start until the transcript is final. Meanwhile the partial transcript has been stable for 400 ms. VoiceMem's streaming architecture calls this speculative prefetch: begin work on a high-confidence partial so the final turn inherits it.

## What to change

- When the partial transcript has been stable above a confidence bar, begin a *provisional* provider call; if the final transcript matches within a normalised edit distance, adopt it, otherwise discard and run normally.
- Never speculative-run a turn that contains a tool call: side effects are not speculations.
- Telemetry records `speculativeStarted`, `speculativeAdopted`, `speculativeDiscarded` — the discard rate is the honest cost of the technique.
- A per-minute cap so a talkative user cannot spin the local model continuously.

**Safety:** speculation must be invisible when wrong and free when right. Any observable side effect disqualifies it.

## Performance contract

- **Baseline:** not implemented — prefill begins only after the final transcript; the item must first record the real time-to-first-token p50 with `voice-01`'s harness, using its 700 ms ceiling as the starting figure
- **Target:** time-to-first-token p50 drops 30% or more on the stable-partial corpus, with adoption rate at or above 60%
- **Must not regress:** must not increase wrong-answer rate by more than 1 percentage point on the fixed evaluation set

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] No tool call is ever issued speculatively
- [ ] A discarded speculation leaves no trace in the conversation history
- [ ] The per-minute cap is enforced and visible in telemetry
- [ ] Disabling the feature returns exactly today's timings

## How to verify

```bash
node --test test/agent.test.js test/router.test.js
node --test --test-concurrency=4
```

## Time estimate

~5-7 days

items.title: feat(voice): on-device streaming transcription with no cloud path at all
items.verify:
node --test test/voice.test.js test/audio-input.test.js
node --test --test-concurrency=4 && node scripts/audit.js
items.body:
## Context

The fast path today is the browser's `SpeechRecognition`, which may send audio to the browser vendor — the repo says so plainly. The local path is a whole-clip Whisper POST. So "fast" and "private" are still two different products, and the privacy-first user pays for it in latency.

## What to change

- A local streaming recogniser behind the existing adapter interface: whisper.cpp or sherpa-onnx launched as a local child process, chosen by the user, not bundled.
- Keep the zero-dependency rule: no npm package, no model in git. The doctor detects an installed binary and reports it; absence is a typed, actionable failure.
- Streaming partials with a stable-prefix API so `voice-02` and `duplex-03` can use them without knowing which engine produced them.
- `docs/VOICE.md`: a table of the three paths (browser, local streaming, optional HTTP) with what each can send where.

**Safety:** the local path must be the private one *and* the fast one. If it is slower, it will not be used, and the privacy claim becomes theoretical.

## Performance contract

- **Baseline:** local path is whole-clip with a 5 s deadline; browser path is faster but may leave the device
- **Target:** final transcript 300 ms or less after endpoint, partials every 200 ms, zero network bytes on the local path
- **Must not regress:** must not regress word error rate by more than 2% relative versus the whole-clip baseline on the same corpus

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The local path demonstrably makes no network calls during a transcription
- [ ] A missing binary produces an actionable message and a working fallback, never a hang

## Context

LiveKit's agent stack treats noise cancellation as table stakes, because a laptop microphone in a room with a fan is the normal case, not the edge case. Our analyser graph measures audio but never conditions it, so the recogniser gets whatever the room sounded like.

items.title: feat(voice): transcribe the utterance you got, not a padded 30 seconds
items.body:
## Context

The Whisper family pads every clip to a fixed 30-second window before the encoder runs, so a two-second command costs the same encode as a paragraph. On the hardware this product runs on that is the whole latency difference: published end-of-utterance latency at one second of audio is 401.7 ms for Whisper Small against 65.1 ms for a variable-length streaming encoder of the same class (Moonshine v2 Small), at a *better* word error rate (7.8% vs 8.6%); the gap widens to 2173 ms vs 129.8 ms against Large v3.

`ear-01` makes transcription local and streaming. This item fixes the *model class* assumption underneath it: an encoder that processes only the audio it was given, and a small streaming cache so most of the work happens while the person is still talking.

## What to change

- A bench over the labelled corpus that reports, per clip length bucket (1–2 s, 3–5 s, >5 s): transcript latency p50/p95 and WER, for the current path and for a variable-length streaming candidate.
- Adopt a candidate only if it wins on both axes at 1–3 s; otherwise publish the measurement and close the item as a documented negative result — a slower model with better numbers in a different bucket is not a win.
- Keep the existing Whisper path as the fallback and as the accuracy reference; the choice is configuration, not a rewrite of `src/voice.js`.
- Streaming partials cached across chunks, with the final transcript still emitted once, unchanged in shape.
- `docs/VOICE.md`: which encoder runs where, and that the improvement claim is scoped to short utterances.

**Safety:** audio stays on the device and inside the existing opt-in; no cloud STT path is added, no always-on capture, and the microphone gate and its visible state are untouched. A model that cannot run on this machine is reported, never silently replaced by a network call.

## Performance contract

- **Baseline:** not implemented — the configured Whisper path pads every clip into a fixed 30-second window, so short commands pay the same encoder cost as long ones (reference: 401.7 ms vs 65.1 ms time-to-first-token at 1 s audio; WER 8.6% vs 7.8%)
- **Target:** short-utterance (1–3 s) transcript latency p50 **at or below 200 ms** with WER within 1 percentage point of today's baseline on the labelled corpus, and time-to-first-token that stops scaling with a padding window
- **Must not regress:** WER may not get worse beyond 1 pp; no audio may leave the machine; the existing Whisper path must remain selectable and the microphone permission model may not change

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The bench reports latency and WER per clip-length bucket for both paths
- [ ] The short-utterance p50 target is met on this machine, not on a vendor's
- [ ] A negative result is published and the item closed rather than the target being quietly widened
- [ ] Final transcript shape, streaming partials and the mic gate are unchanged for callers
- [ ] Zero network bytes are attributable to transcription

## How to verify

```bash
node --test test/voice.test.js
node --test --test-concurrency=4 && node scripts/audit.js
```

## Time estimate

~1-2 weeks

items.body:
## Context

This is the item the rest of the frontier exists to make possible, and the one that is not available anywhere today in a local-first personal assistant.

Three products each solve a third of it. OpenAdapt records a task once and compiles it into a program that runs with no model calls and no screenshots leaving the machine — but you record it by hand, and the program is not conversational. OpenClaw has skills, but they are written instructions a model re-reads every time, so they are as slow and as variable as the model. Pipecat and LiveKit give you a fast voice loop with no memory of how a task was done.

Quasnooze already has the two halves that no one has joined: a tool trace with typed results (`src/agent.js`) and an undo journal (`laptop-05`). Join them and a successful task becomes a program, proposed in conversation, approved by the user, replayable in milliseconds.

## What to change

- Capture: after a multi-step turn that succeeded, keep the ordered `(tool, arguments, verified result)` trace, including the preconditions the trace observed (window focused, file existed, volume was X).
- Compile: propose a named skill with the recorded calls as literals plus declared parameters, its preconditions, its postconditions, and the undo plan. Show it as a diff a person can edit before saving.
- Replay: execute without a model call when every precondition holds; the same risk classifier and approval gates apply per call as before, and a skill cannot grant permissions it was not approved with.
- Storage: a JSON file next to the existing custom-tool config, diffable and reviewable, with a version and the turn it was compiled from.

**Safety:** a compiled skill is code that runs on the user's machine. It is shown before it is saved, it is editable as text, and it never gains a permission the original turn did not have.

## Performance contract

- **Baseline:** every repetition of a known task costs a full model turn (4-8 s and tokens) and can vary between runs
- **Target:** replay p50 under 300 ms with zero model calls for a five-step skill, and byte-identical tool arguments across runs
- **Must not regress:** must not reduce tool-call accuracy: a compiled skill must reproduce the approved trace exactly or refuse to run

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A compiled skill never contains a destructive step that was not in the approved trace
- [ ] Every replay still passes the risk classifier, and `act` steps still ask
- [ ] Editing one literal in the JSON changes exactly that literal on the next replay
- [ ] A skill refuses to run when its declared preconditions do not hold, and says which one failed
- [ ] The trace records no message text, only tool names, arguments and results

## How to verify

```bash
node --test test/custom-tools.test.js test/agent.test.js
node --test --test-concurrency=4 && node scripts/audit.js
```

## Time estimate

~2-3 weeks

items.verify:

node --test --test-concurrency=4 && node scripts/audit.js
items.body:
## Context

OpenAdapt's benchmark is the argument for this feature: an agent acting alone was right 62 times out of 63 and *looked* right every time, while a verified program was right 18 of 18 and stopped when it could not confirm. Confidence is not correctness, and a tool returning `ok: true` only means the call did not throw.

`reason-01` checks that a claim matches the receipts. This goes further: it makes the receipt itself an observation of the outside world.

## What to change

- A postcondition per tool family, checked against the system rather than the call: file exists at the destination and its hash matches, window title is focused, volume level reads back, clipboard content equals what was written.
- A three-valued outcome — `verified`, `unverified`, `contradicted` — instead of a boolean, surfaced in the transcript so an unverified step is visibly unverified.
- A `contradicted` step halts the remaining plan and reports the divergence, rather than continuing on a false premise.
- `docs/ACTION-PREVIEWS.md`: postconditions appear in the preview, so approval covers the check as well as the action.

**Safety:** verification is not permission: reading state back must not require new privileges, and a verified action is still an approved action.

## Performance contract

- **Baseline:** not implemented — success is asserted from a tool's return value, so a silently failed action is reported as done; 0 observed steps carry an independent read-back
- **Target:** zero silent wrong-success claims across a 20-case fault-injection suite, with verified steps at 95% or more on the happy path
- **Must not regress:** must not add more than 50 ms p95 per step for local read-backs

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A contradicted postcondition stops the plan and names the mismatch — **partially done**: the contradiction is handed to the model and shown to the user, but the tool loop is not force-stopped; stopping the plan belongs to the compiled-skill replay in `skill-01`
- [x] An unreadable state reports `unverified`, never `verified`
- [x] Fault injection (file vanished, window closed, write reverted) is covered by tests
- [x] Read-back cost stays inside the stated budget

## How to verify

```bash
node --test test/agent.test.js test/action-preview.test.js
node --test --test-concurrency=4
```

## Time estimate

~1-2 weeks
## Outcome — shipped 2026-11-05

`src/verify.js` gives every tool result a three-state verdict — `verified`,
`contradicted`, `unverified` — from an independent read of the world rather than
the tool's own return value. What is covered today: file writes (byte-for-byte
read-back), arithmetic (recomputation), tasks, reminders and remembered facts
(the store is the record). Everything else is honestly `unverified`.

Measured in `docs/VERIFIED-EXECUTION.md`:

- 20 injected faults, **20 correct verdicts**, **0 silent wrong successes** — a
  write that never landed, a truncated write, a sum that does not recompute, a
  task that is not in the list, a reminder that was never stored.
- Read-back cost: **p50 0.28 ms, p95 0.69 ms** for a 2 KB file write;
  p95 0.02 ms for arithmetic. The contract allowed 50 ms.
- A contradiction travels two ways: into the tool message so the model cannot
  describe the action as done, and into the reply as a visible warning. The
  user does not depend on the model repeating it.

Two honest gaps. A verifier that throws is `unverified`, never `verified` —
tested — but the loop keeps going rather than stopping the plan, which matters
once a compiled skill has a plan to stop. And `shell` stays `unverified` by
design: an exit code is the tool's own report, not the world's.

items.body:
## Context

The failure mode that kills recorded macros is drift: an app updates, a button moves, a file is named differently, and the recorded program does something adjacent and wrong. OpenAdapt's answer is to stop and tell the agent rather than guess; ours has to be the same, because a skill that misapplies is worse than no skill.

## What to change

- Precondition diffing at replay time: name the specific precondition that failed and what it expects versus what it found.
- Two bounded repairs, in order: re-resolve a named target by the same fuzzy-but-visible matching used for windows, or hand the diff back to the model for a single re-plan. If both fail, stop with the diff.
- A drift record per skill (last failure, failing precondition, count) so a skill that keeps drifting is visibly unreliable and can be quarantined.
- Never silently widen a target: if a file match goes from one candidate to three, ask.

**Safety:** recovering is optional; misapplying is not permitted. When in doubt, stop.

## Performance contract

- **Baseline:** not implemented — a stale skill either fails obscurely or applies to the wrong target; there is no precondition list to compare against, so drift is undetectable in 1 run out of 1
- **Target:** 90% or more of drifted replay attempts either recover correctly or stop with a named precondition, and zero misapplied runs in the drift suite
- **Must not regress:** must not regress replay latency on the non-drifted path

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Every drift produces a diff naming expected versus found
- [ ] Ambiguity (more than one candidate) always asks instead of picking
- [ ] A quarantined skill is refused with the reason attached
- [ ] No repair path bypasses approval for an `act` step

```bash
node --test test/custom-tools.test.js test/agent.test.js

```

## Time estimate

~1-2 weeks

## Context

"Louder." "Open Slack." "Pause." do not need a 7B model. Routing every utterance through one is why local assistants feel slower than their hardware should allow, and it also wastes tokens on requests whose entire meaning fits in a grammar. `src/router.js` already decides provider routing; this adds a deterministic intent tier in front of generation.

## What to change

- A hand-written grammar and matcher for the machine-intent classes the tools already provide: media, volume, launch/focus, lock/sleep, timer, clipboard read. Deterministic, inspectable, testable.
- A confidence floor and a mandatory fallback: anything unmatched or ambiguous goes to the model unchanged.
- The matcher never invents arguments. A phrase it cannot fill completely falls through, so "open the thing from yesterday" is a model request, not a guess.
- The transcript says which path answered, so a fast path that got it wrong is visible immediately.

**Safety:** a fast wrong action is worse than a slow right one. Approvals still apply, and the fallback is not allowed to be lossy.

## Performance contract

- **Baseline:** every turn goes through generation; p50 700 ms plus model time for a one-word request
- **Target:** p50 under 400 ms end-to-end for matched intents at 95% or higher routing accuracy on a labelled set of 200 utterances
- **Must not regress:** must not reduce answer quality: unmatched or ambiguous utterances must fall through at 100%, and the model path must remain byte-identical

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] Ambiguous and out-of-grammar utterances fall through, verified case by case
- [x] The same risk tiers and approvals apply to fast-path actions
- [ ] The labelled set reaches 200 utterances and its misses are published in full — **partially done**: 59 labelled utterances (31 positive, 28 negative), 100% of the positives matched, 0 of the negatives routed
- [x] Disabling the fast path returns exactly today's behaviour

## How to verify

```bash
node --test test/router.test.js test/agent.test.js
node --test --test-concurrency=4
```

## Time estimate

~4-6 days
## Outcome — shipped 2026-11-05

Landed in `src/fast-path.js` with `test/fast-path.test.js` (11 tests) and the
measurement in `docs/FAST-PATH-EVAL.md`.

- Matcher decision: p50 5 µs. Whole fast turn end to end: p50 4.3 ms, p95 7.9 ms
  (n = 50), including the tool run, the honesty guard, the session write and
  telemetry — against a ≥ 700 ms model-turn floor.
- Routing: 31/31 intended phrasings matched, 0/28 neighbouring phrasings routed.
  Every one of the 28 is a sentence where acting would have been a guess:
  "remember to buy milk", "remind me to call mom" (no time), "add a task to buy
  milk and then remind me at 5pm".
- The allowlist is five tools (`time_now`, `calculator`, `remember`, `add_task`,
  `remind`); a failed tool call falls through to the model instead of returning
  an error; unattended runs and attachment-bearing turns never take it;
  `QUASNOOZE_FAST_PATH=off` restores the previous behaviour exactly.
- Found and fixed a real bug in the tool it calls: `parseClock("99pm")` used to
  roll over into a reminder four days later.

The honest gap: the target asked for 200 utterances. This ships 59, written by
the author of the matcher, so it establishes that the rules fire as specified —
not how often a stranger phrases the same request. Expanding the set from real
transcripts is tracked by `voice-05-stt-accuracy-harness`.

## Context

Prefill is the dominant cost of a local turn, and it grows with the conversation. By turn twenty the assistant is slower than it was at turn one for no reason the user can see. items.body:
## Context

Prefill, not generation, is what makes a local assistant feel slow: every turn re-processes the system prompt, the tool schemas and the conversation before the first new token exists. llama.cpp and its downstreams keep the KV cache for a shared prefix, so the turn can resume instead of re-reading. Two things in this checkout defeat that reuse:

- `src/prompt.js:50` puts `Date and time: <now>` and up to forty remembered facts into the *system* prompt — the first bytes of every request. A minute boundary, a new fact or a changed workspace list invalidates the whole cache behind it.
- `src/brain.js:143` sends `options: { temperature, num_ctx, num_predict }` and no `keep_alive`, so Ollama unloads the model — and dumps the cache — after its default five idle minutes.

Published measurements put the size of the prize at 8x–17x on prompt-eval time for a warm prefix (962 ms cold vs 54 ms warm for a 723-token prompt; up to 93% TTFT reduction with host-RAM prefix caching). This is the cheapest large win on fixed hardware and needs no new dependency.

## What to change

- A canonical prompt builder: one function, one serialisation, static block first (identity, rules, tool list in a deterministic order), then volatile content (time, recalled facts, task) at the tail. A test asserts the byte-identical prefix across two turns in the same minute.
- Move the clock out of the prefix: keep `time_now` as a tool and the fast path (`mind-01`) as the way to ask the time, and pass the date only when the turn needs it.
- A bounded `keep_alive` (default 30 minutes, configurable, `0` restores today's behaviour exactly) sent on every Ollama request.
- Record `prompt_eval_duration`, `prompt_eval_count` and the derived cache-hit ratio per turn in `src/telemetry.js`, so the claim is a number in the panel rather than a feeling.
- `docs/GUIDE.md`: what is cached, what invalidates it, and how to read the hit ratio.

**Safety:** no new network, no new runtime dependency, no change to what the model is told. `keep_alive` is bounded rather than infinite so a personal laptop is never pinned by the assistant; the setting is documented and user-visible.

## Performance contract

- **Baseline:** not instrumented — the system prompt carries a minute-resolution timestamp and up to 40 memory facts ahead of the task, `src/brain.js` sends no `keep_alive`, and Ollama's default five-minute unload discards the KV cache. A cold re-prefill therefore pays the whole prefix on the first turn after any idle gap or any minute boundary (reference measurement for the same shape of prompt: 962 ms cold vs 54 ms warm prompt-eval, 17.7x)
- **Target:** multi-turn prefill p50 down **60% or more from turn 2 onward**, cache-hit ratio above 85% at steady state, with a test that proves the prefix is byte-identical across consecutive turns in the same minute
- **Must not regress:** the model must still know today's date when a turn needs it (a date-rollover test fails the build if the clock is simply deleted), recalled facts must remain available, and a cold first turn may not get slower

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Two consecutive turns produce a byte-identical static prefix, asserted by test
- [ ] Prefill p50 is down 60% or more at turn 2 on the recorded baseline script
- [ ] `keep_alive` is configurable, bounded, and `0` restores exact current behaviour
- [ ] Cache-hit ratio is visible in telemetry and `npm run health`
- [ ] A date-rollover test still returns the correct date through the tool and the fast path
- [ ] No new dependency and no change to the tool schemas the model receives

## How to verify

```bash
node --test test/agent.test.js test/router.test.js
node --test --test-concurrency=4 && node scripts/audit.js
```

## Time estimate

~3-5 days
